final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced

**Expected:** `eslint ./ --fix` fixes every file with auto-fixable problems and exits 0.

**Actual:** The run aborts with `Error: EMFILE: too many open files, open '.../src/f543.js'`. The stack is the one in the report: `fs.promises.writeFile`, then `Promise.all (index N)`, then `ESLint.outputFixes (lib/eslint/eslint.js:533)`, then `cli.js:637`. ESLint exits 2. Only about as many files as the fd limit get written. With 1000 files and a limit of 512, 508 files were left unfixed.

**Trigger:** More files with a fix to write than the process's open-file limit. `outputFixes` starts all the `writeFile` calls at once with `Promise.all`, so every file is opened before any is closed. One rule (`no-var` or `semi`) and trivial files are enough.

**Run:** `bash repro/emfile-fix.sh` from the repo root. It builds a temp project of 1000 files, each containing `var a = 1;\nconsole.log(a)`, and runs `bin/eslint.js ./ --fix` with `ulimit -n 512`. It exits 1 if eslint exits non-zero or any file is still unfixed, and 0 otherwise. `FILES` and `FD_LIMIT` override the defaults.

**Passes when:** The same script with `FD_LIMIT=20000`, so the limit is above the file count, passes: eslint exits 0 and no files are left unfixed.

**Reliability:** The check failed 10/10 times at the defaults. Two other runs also failed: a manual run with 3000 files at `ulimit -n 1024` (1/1), and a run with 25000 files at this machine's own default limit of 20000 (1/1). The last needs no lowered limit and fails at `Promise.all (index 19980)`, but takes about 60s.

**Artifacts:** `/work/runs/a8cb098daf/repo/repro/emfile-fix.sh`. The scratch projects are in `/tmp/fx1` and `/tmp/fx2` and can be deleted.

Windows was not available. The check lowers the Linux fd limit to stand in for the lower limit on the reporter's machine, so on Windows it is simulated. The 25000-file run at the default limit is real on Linux. ESLint here is 9.30.1 from the checkout, not the reporter's 9.28.0. No production code was changed; the only change in the working tree is the new `repro/` directory.
patch:
diff --git a/repro/emfile-fix.sh b/repro/emfile-fix.sh
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..95227c4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/repro/emfile-fix.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Check: `eslint ./ --fix` over more auto-fixable files than the process may
+# hold open file descriptors must fix every file and exit 0 (no EMFILE).
+#
+# Run from the repo root:  bash repro/emfile-fix.sh
+#
+# FILES    number of files with an auto-fixable problem (default 1000)
+# FD_LIMIT soft open-file limit for the eslint process (default 512, simulating
+#          the lower per-process limit on the reporter's Windows machine;
+#          the same failure happens at this machine's default limit of 20000
+#          with FILES=25000, just much slower)
+#
+# Exit status: 0 when all files were fixed and eslint exited 0; non-zero otherwise.
+set -u
+
+REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+FILES="${FILES:-1000}"
+FD_LIMIT="${FD_LIMIT:-512}"
+
+WORK="$(mktemp -d /tmp/eslint-emfile-XXXXXX)" || exit 2
+trap '[ -n "${WORK:-}" ] && [ -d "$WORK" ] && rm -rf -- "$WORK"' EXIT
+
+mkdir -p "$WORK/src"
+cat > "$WORK/eslint.config.js" <<'EOF'
+module.exports = [{ rules: { semi: "error", "no-var": "error" } }];
+EOF
+
+i=1
+while [ "$i" -le "$FILES" ]; do
+    printf 'var a = 1;\nconsole.log(a)\n' > "$WORK/src/f$i.js"
+    i=$((i + 1))
+done
+
+cd "$WORK" || exit 2
+(
+    ulimit -n "$FD_LIMIT" || exit 2
+    node "$REPO_ROOT/bin/eslint.js" ./ --fix > "$WORK/eslint.out" 2>&1
+)
+status=$?
+
+# Count files that still contain the unfixed `var`.
+unfixed="$(grep -l '^var ' "$WORK"/src/*.js | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
+
+echo "files=$FILES fd_limit=$FD_LIMIT eslint_exit=$status unfixed_files=$unfixed"
+grep -m1 'EMFILE' "$WORK/eslint.out" || true
+
+if [ "$status" -ne 0 ] || [ "$unfixed" -ne 0 ]; then
+    echo "FAIL: expected every file fixed and exit 0" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+echo "PASS"
